analysis.title: 3Q26 Sector Preview: Constructive Setup Intact as Supply Constraints, AI Momentum, and Cyclical Recovery Support Further Revisions / Continued Equity Outperformance
key_insights: JPM enters 3Q26 earnings season constructive but selective on semis and semicap. SMH is up 68% YTD, driven by AI infrastructure spend, supply tightness and a broadening cyclical recovery. Top picks are AVGO and MRVL.

The focus this quarter shifts from demand, which is well understood, to supply: where constraints are most acute (leading-edge foundry, memory, HBM, advanced packaging, power), how long they last, and when capacity can ease them.
Other OW names highlighted: NVDA and AMD in compute, MU and SNDK in memory, TXN and ADI in analog, AMAT, LRCX and KLAC in semicap. Smid-cap preferences are ALAB, AMKR and MKSI.

Street cloud capex (hyperscalers plus neoclouds) for CY26/CY27/CY28 is $950B/$1.42T/$1.55T, up 97%/47%/9% Y/Y. JPM expects NVDA, AMD, AVGO and MRVL to point to upside to backlog and order visibility into CY27.

Custom XPUs/ASICs are taking share of AI accelerator units, from about 32% in CY25 to about 43% in CY26E and 56% in CY27E. AVGO and MRVL are the best-positioned beneficiaries alongside NVDA (merchant GPU) and AMD (MI4xx/MI5xx).

Networking is one of the fastest-growing layers of the AI stack. JPM's hardware team models AI DC switch markets growing at 31%/36%/43%/42% CAGRs through CY30, driven by the 800G to 1.6T transition and Ethernet share gains.

Server CPU demand is accelerating on agentic AI inference workloads, with TAM CAGR above 50% through 2030. AMD is gaining share from INTC (about 41% x86 server CPU revenue share in 2Q26, 60%+ revenue CAGR for AMD vs mid-50s% TAM growth).

PC unit shipments are expected to decline HSD%/LDD% Y/Y in CY26 on memory-driven BOM inflation, after above-seasonal 1H26 pull-forward. Commentary is expected to be cautious for consumer-levered names such as INTC's PC segment.

Analog: demand is improving with supply tightness and pricing is becoming a tailwind (ADI additional increases, TXN select increases in Q4 and broader increases planned for next year). Broad restocking has not fully occurred and the macro backdrop is more uncertain over the last ~90 days. ADI and TXN are preferred.

Memory: JPM's global team sees a ~20%/~19%/~15% shortage in CY26/27/28 even after despec, with accumulated HBM shortage reaching 23 weeks by CY28. MU says CY27 and CY28 run significantly tighter than CY26.

MU stepped up to 26 SCAs (from 16) covering 35%+ of revenue through 2030, with $150B RPO and $32B customer cash commitments. Over 75% of FY27 output is committed, and new SCAs are signed at current elevated pricing, re-anchoring the through-cycle gross margin floor (~62% reference).

HBM enters a new pricing regime in CY27, with CY27 HBM pricing 'significantly higher' Y/Y resetting Jan-1. JPM forecasts blended HBM pricing +54%/+25% Y/Y in CY27/CY28 and HBM TAM of ~$160B/~$280B in CY27/28 from ~$64B in CY26.

MU's F4Q26 data center SSD revenue was about $10B, 10x Y/Y, on KV-cache offload and HDD displacement. MU FY27 capex is above $55B vs about $27B in FY26, and MU will return 100% of excess cash after the 12/9/26 CHIPS anniversary, with a larger buyback authorization expected imminently.

Semicap: JPM models WFE +31% Y/Y in 2026 to $163B, +38% in 2027 to $225B, and +17% in 2028 to $263B. Foundry/logic and DRAM drive the upside and NAND is more measured. The debate is whether revenue revisions continue or cleanroom readiness limits conversion of demand into shipments.

KLAC is the preferred large-cap semicap name on relative underperformance (+66% YTD vs LRCX +91%, AMAT +102%, ONTO +91%) and underappreciated leverage to 2027 foundry/logic WFE and process complexity.

TSMC capex is estimated by JPM's global team at $64B/$86B/$100B in 2026/27/28. INTC and Terafab are potential incremental foundry/logic WFE sources but with uncertain timing. JPM forecasts DRAM capex of about $413B over 2026-2028, up from about $368B.
WSTS data show QTD semi sales up 24% Q/Q and 17% Q/Q ex-memory through July and August, vs seasonal norms of 7% and 8%. Total semis revenue was up 156% Y/Y in August and ex-memory up 45% Y/Y.
The share of covered companies with positive earnings revisions has stayed above 70% over the past several earnings seasons, and JPM expects this to continue.

Auto semis: JPM is cautious into 3Q. S&P Mobility sees global light vehicle production down 2% Y/Y in 3Q26, so content gains must offset weak units. JPM prefers TXN and ADI over auto-levered NXPI and ON.
Industrial semis are a cleaner recovery than auto, driven by energy infrastructure, A&D, factory automation, medical and data-center power. TXN, ADI and MCHP are preferred.

EDA/IP: CDNS and SNPS should deliver constructive results. CDNS backlog exited 2Q at a record $8.1B. SNPS targets a ~15% FY26-FY30E revenue CAGR and ~50% non-GAAP operating margin by FY30E, and has a $1B multi-year IP agreement with Amazon.
MRVL's Investor Day guided interconnect revenue to potentially reach about $37.5B by 2030. JPM forecasts MRVL optical interconnect revenue +84% Y/Y this year and +82% in 2027.

AVGO has about 70% share of hyperscaler switching/routing silicon. AI networking revenue rose more than 2.5x Y/Y last quarter, and JPM sees this as underappreciated versus the custom silicon displacement debate.

IDC forecasts 2026 global smartphone shipments down 16.7% Y/Y, with 2H26 down 27% as NAND/DRAM costs run +300% Y/Y. Revenue TAM is still expected up 6% on higher ASPs. Apple is the main beneficiary (iOS shipments -1.3% vs Android -24.3%).

JPM sees continued semi M&A supporting valuations. Semi and semicap deal volume was about $47B in 2025. Recent deals include NVDA/Hugging Face ($11.9B), AMD/World Labs ($8.2B) and TXN/Silicon Labs ($7.2B).

sector_views.rationale: Constructive but selective. AI infrastructure investment, supply tightness and cyclical recovery support further positive revisions.
WFE is modeled +31% in 2026, +38% in 2027 and +17% in 2028. The key risk is cleanroom readiness limiting conversion.
Shortage deepening through CY28, SCA/LTA coverage building, HBM repricing and a possible re-rating.
Demand and pricing improving, channel inventories lean, with a preference for industrial, A&D and data-center exposure.
Mixed view. Content gains offset weak units, and light vehicle production is expected down 2% Y/Y in 3Q26.
Memory cost inflation is cutting smartphone units, with IDC forecasting -16.7% in 2026. Scaled premium OEMs and their suppliers are favored.
Rising chip complexity, hyperscaler custom silicon and 3DIC support demand. Agentic AI is expected to expand rather than compress EDA.

earnings_insights: JPM 3Q26E vs consensus revenue (estimates, not reported): AMAT $9,115M vs consensus $10,275M (-11.3%), ARM $1,289M vs $1,377M (-6.4%), NVDA $109,219M vs $108,836M (+0.4%), AVGO $34,800M vs $34,822M (-0.1%), MRVL $3,150M vs $3,155M (-0.2%).

JPM 3Q26E vs consensus non-GAAP EPS (estimates, not reported): AMAT $3.50 vs $4.06 (-13.8%), SNDK $49.81 vs $45.95 (+8.4%), AMKR $0.82 vs $0.76 (+7.8%), SYNA $1.36 vs $1.26 (+7.8%), NVDA $2.48 vs $2.48, AVGO $3.81 vs $3.83, MRVL $1.10 vs $1.11.
JPM 4Q26E revenue vs consensus (estimates): SWKS $1,090M vs $1,276M (-14.6%), ARM $1,382M vs $1,531M (-9.8%), AMD $15,715M vs $16,275M (-3.4%), MTSI $448M vs $428M (+4.6%).

CDNS: JPM models 3Q26 revenue of $1.61B and EPS of $2.04 (estimates) vs consensus of $1.61B and $2.05. Company guidance is 3Q revenue about $1.61B, EPS about $2.04, FY26 revenue about $6.3B and EPS about $8.10.
SNPS: JPM models F4Q26 revenue of $2.61B and EPS of $4.25 (estimates) vs consensus of $2.62B and $4.44.

Semis earnings revisions have been positive for more than 70% of covered companies over several seasons. JPM expects most covered companies to deliver solid 3Q results and constructive 4Q/CY27 commentary.
Semicap companies usually give formal out-year WFE guidance in Q4, so JPM does not expect a full 2027 framework this quarter.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Well above seasonal norms of +7% and +8%, a constructive read-through for 3Q revenue.
Sales, units and ASPs are all accelerating. Memory pricing drives most of the growth, but ex-memory is also strong.
Growth of +97%/+47%/+9% Y/Y. It underpins AI semiconductor demand, with growth decelerating after CY27.
Growth of +31%/+38%/+17% Y/Y, driven by foundry/logic and DRAM.

macro_indicators.indicator: Global light vehicle production (S&P Global Mobility)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Incrementally worse than July expectations, a headwind for auto-levered semis.
Memory cost inflation of +300%+ Y/Y pressures low-end Android, with 2H26 shipments down 27%.
Sustained supply deficit supports pricing and the memory re-rating thesis.

trade_ideas.description: Long KLAC as the preferred large-cap semicap name
trade_ideas.rationale: Relative underperformance YTD, underappreciated leverage to 2027 foundry/logic WFE and room for consensus revenue revisions.
trade_ideas.risk: Cleanroom constraints could limit conversion of demand into shipments.

trade_ideas.description: Long AVGO and MRVL as top picks in semis
trade_ideas.rationale: Best positioned custom XPU and networking beneficiaries as XPU share of accelerator units rises.
trade_ideas.risk: Supply-chain capacity gating and the pace of CY27+ capex sustainability.

trade_ideas.description: Long memory (MU, SNDK) into the re-rating on SCA/LTA disclosure
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural supply-demand tightness and business model change, with a possible sector-wide re-rating from more SCA/LTA disclosure.

trade_ideas.description: Long ADI and TXN in analog
trade_ideas.rationale: Broad exposure to durable demand in industrial, A&D and data-center-adjacent power, plus pricing increases.
trade_ideas.risk: Customers may keep buying to current consumption rather than replenishing inventories.

risk_factors: Supply-chain capacity gating (leading-edge foundry, HBM, advanced packaging, power) limits near-term growth.
The pace of CY27+ cloud capex sustainability.
Cleanroom and facility readiness may slow conversion of WFE demand into shipments.
Memory-driven BOM inflation pressures PCs and smartphones, especially low-end Android.
The macro backdrop has become more uncertain over the last ~90 days, which may keep analog customers from restocking.
Auto semis face declining global light vehicle production.
Competitive displacement concerns in AVGO's custom silicon business.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong tool demand, extended orderbook visibility and customer urgency support continued upward revisions to out-quarter revenue. JPM models WFE +38% in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Cleanroom and facility readiness may slow the conversion of demand into shipments and revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Companies stop revising out-quarter revenue above Street estimates, or cite cleanroom constraints limiting shipments, in this earnings season.

tension_points.bull_case: Improving orders, lean channel inventories, firmer lead times and price increases could drive broader replenishment into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A more uncertain macro backdrop may keep customers buying to current consumption rather than restocking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 4Q guides showing demand staying near run-rate consumption rather than broad replenishment.

tension_points.bull_case: Improving backlog, lengthening commitments and expanding cloud profitability support elevated capex through CY28 and beyond.
tension_points.bear_case: Supply-chain capacity gating and the pace of CY27+ capex sustainability, with Street cloud capex growth slowing to +9% in CY28.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler commentary pointing to slower CY27 order visibility.

tension_points.bull_case: AVGO adds XPU customers and lengthens multi-year commitments, and its networking business grows as fast as XPUs.
tension_points.bear_case: Competitive displacement concerns in custom silicon / XPUs dominate the stock debate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of XPU customer displacement in the upcoming results.
